model: Cummins PowerCommand CCM-G genset monitoring via BASgatewayLX
applies_to: Cummins generator sets monitored by a PowerCommand CCM-G (through the Cummins Modbus/LonWorks gateway), read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the Cummins CCM-G: 415 objects (255 AI, 160 BI), 83 polled by default. The map repeats one block per genset (Gen 0 to Gen 3): name, control switch, state, fault code and type, kW, frequency, PF, voltages, currents, engine values, counters and the annunciator bits. Only Gen 0 is polled by default.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile Cummins_Single_PowCmd_CCM_G_Genset_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the Cummins ModLon gateway Modbus map (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/MODLON_Gateway.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 83 of the 415 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (Gen 0 Total kW; Gen 1 Total kW; Gen 2 Total kW...); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.

integration.summary: Read Gen 0 state, running and supplying-load bits, kW and fault code; enable the Gen 1-3 blocks for more gensets.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Gen 0 Start/Stop and Reset (AI 50, AI 51) are inputs here, so they cannot be written.
Units in the Gen 0 block are partly off (e.g. Amps a shows volts); trust the names.
Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
